instruction: GUI-only requirement: Complete the task entirely in the opened Blender graphical user interface. Do not open Command Prompt, PowerShell, Terminal, or any shell; do not run Python, bpy scripts, Text Editor scripts, Geometry Nodes exported scripts, or blender --background automation that directly generates or edits the deliverable files. Do not install or run helper add-ons that auto-build the required result. Use only Blender native GUI tools, menus, editors, and built-in save/export commands. External Helical Thread `scene.blend` contains a single mesh object `Shaft` - a smooth cylindrical shaft coaxial with the world Z axis. Cut a continuous helical groove into the top 2 BU of the shaft so that the lower portion remains an untouched smooth cylinder. Save the result as `answer.blend`. Groove parameters - Thread region: the upper 2 BU of the shaft (top 40% of the axial length). - Pitch (lead): 0.5 BU of axial travel per full 360 deg turn. - Groove cross-section: circular, radius 0.05 BU. - Exactly four complete turns over the thread region; helix starts at the lower edge of the region and ends at the top face. - Subtractive only: the groove removes material. No geometry extends beyond the original cylindrical envelope. Requirements: 1. The scene contains a mesh object named `Shaft`. 2. Exactly one mesh object exists in the scene. 3. The object's world location and rotation are unchanged from the initial scene. 4. The mesh is closed-manifold (every edge shared by exactly two faces). 5. The axial extent of the mesh is unchanged (z from 0 to 5 within tol). 6. The lower portion of the shaft (z in [0.5, 2.5]) is still a smooth cylinder at the original radius. 7. Inside the thread region the groove cuts at least one full groove-radius below the shaft surface. 8. Inside the thread region the crest of the thread still reaches the original shaft radius. 9. The groove follows a right-handed helix whose angular position advances consistently with the specified pitch across the thread region. Inspect the initial mesh to read off shaft radius, length, and orientation before cutting.
